note: Emitted for the Agda track (agda/OBLIGATIONS.md is owned by the Agda track; entries go through Hilbert). 'runtime_checked' means the Rust authority enforces it with a runtime check and the adversarial suite exercises it. It is NOT a machine-checked proof. Assumptions are never discharged here.

agda_alignment.source: /workspace/jwst-lrd-agda-kernel/agda/kernel/src/Kernel/Assumptions/{Crypto,Runtime}.agda (branch t011-agda-kernel, uncommitted working tree, read-only, observed 2026-10-19)

witness_contract.name: verify_witness
witness_contract.semantics: true iff 0 < w < N and w^{H_prime(domain, element)} == acc_value (mod N); H_prime recomputed by the verifier
witness_contract.replace_with: the canonical ledger accumulator when it lands (t005-rsaacc ledger/rsaacc had uncommitted work only, when this was written)

obligations.name: CapabilityConsumedOnce
obligations.statement: Each transition capability id appears at most once in the consumed log; it is consumed (status=consumed, added to the retired accumulator, persisted) on its first authenticated SUBMIT, whether that SUBMIT is accepted or rejected.
obligations.rust: authority.rs Authority::submit step 3 (retire(idx, Consumed) + persist), check_cap (Consumed => replay)

obligations.name: MonotonicCounter
obligations.statement: The authority counter (head seq) increases by exactly 1 on each ACCEPT, is unchanged on REJECT, and the persisted counter never decreases, including across restarts. Over the trace of accepted states it is strictly increasing (the Agda form c t < c (suc t)).
obligations.rust: authority.rs persist_inner (in-memory and on-disk monotonicity guard, write-temp+fsync+rename+fsync dir), load (counter == chain length - 1), init (refuses to re-initialize)

obligations.name: NoRollback
obligations.statement: A proposal is accepted only if seq == authority_seq + 1 and prev_commit == authority head commitment; seq <= authority_seq yields stale_seq, a gap yields seq_gap, a wrong prev yields bad_prev.

obligations.name: NoReplay
obligations.statement: No capability and no authority nonce is accepted twice: consumed capability => replay; a nonce already bound into an accepted state => replay.

obligations.name: CapabilitySlotBinding
obligations.statement: Linear addressing: a transition capability authorizes exactly the slot (cap_seq, cap_prev) = (head.seq+1, head.commit) at issuance; any other slot yields cap_binding.

obligations.name: HistoricalReadNoTransition
obligations.statement: read / historical_read capabilities grant read access only (bounded by cap_seq) and are rejected with bad_scope by SUBMIT; scope is MAC-bound.

obligations.name: ProofGatedTransition
obligations.statement: SUBMIT requires prev_witness with verify_witness(acc_states, prev_commit, prev_witness) == true, else bad_witness.

obligations.name: RejectNoNewState
obligations.statement: A REJECT decision carries no new_commit and leaves (seq, head, acc_states) unchanged (built with the ledger header's lrd_decision_reject). Only the capability table and the retired accumulator may change on REJECT (the capability is burned).

obligations.name: AuthorityComputesCommitment
obligations.statement: new_commit is computed by the authority as SHA-256("LRD-COMMIT-v1\0" || LRD-REC-v1{cap_nonce, commit=prev_commit, kind=capability, payload_sha256, seq}); a differing worker claim yields bad_commit.

obligations.name: AccumulatorWitnessSound
obligations.statement: If verify_witness(A, x, w) is true then x was added to A. Holds under the strong RSA assumption for a modulus whose factorization nobody knows, with H_prime modelled as a random oracle into 256-bit primes (Miller-Rabin, 40 hash-derived bases).

obligations.name: MACUnforgeable
obligations.statement: HMAC-SHA256 is EUF-CMA secure: without K_auth no party can produce a valid cap_mac for a new capability body.

obligations.name: CollisionResistant
obligations.statement: SHA-256 is collision resistant (commitments bind to seq, prev_commit, payload_sha256, nonce).

obligations.name: CSPRNGFresh
obligations.statement: /dev/urandom outputs are unpredictable to the worker; 256-bit nonces and 128-bit capability ids do not collide (the authority also checks uniqueness).

obligations.name: AuthorityKeyUncompromised
obligations.statement: Only the authority process can read authority.key. NO protection is claimed against an attacker who reads or writes it (see test out_of_scope_key_read_allows_mac_forgery).

obligations.name: CounterStoreUncompromised
obligations.statement: Only the authority process can modify authority.state (counter, head, capability table). NO protection is claimed against an attacker who writes or rolls it back (see test out_of_scope_store_write_allows_rollback_and_replay). A hardware monotonic counter (TPM NV counter / TEE / remote HSM) would be required; none is implemented.

obligations.name: OSProcessIsolation
obligations.statement: The kernel enforces process memory isolation and file permissions between the worker and the authority, and Unix socket endpoints are not impersonated. Root or kernel compromise breaks every guarantee here. In the tests both processes run as the same uid, so the separation is by convention (separate directories) and NOT enforced by the OS.

obligations.name: TrustedSetupRSAModulus
obligations.statement: Nobody knows the factorization of N. Test moduli come from openssl genrsa with the key deleted afterwards; this is NOT a trustworthy setup ceremony.
